Hi all,

Thanks for taking the time earlier this week to chat about partner integration options. I wanted to follow up with a concise scoping note so we can align on next steps and owners. Goal: land a partnered integration story that supports Redwood customers who want managed vector DBs (Pinecone/Weaviate) with S3-based cold storage as a fallback for very large collections.

Proposed agenda for a 30–45 min technical kickoff:
- Brief intros & use-cases from partner/customer POV (5–10m)
- Auth & networking patterns (VPC peering, API keys, role-based access) (10m)
- Data sync & ingestion patterns (real-time vs batch; upsert semantics) (10m)
- POC success criteria & timeline (10m)

Immediate asks:
1) Can Pinecone/Weaviate confirm recommended auth flow for server-side inference connections (API key + optional IP allowlist / service account)?
2) Any rate-limit/throughput guidance for a 50–200 QPS production footprint?
3) Samir, if VectorWorks were to run the POC, can you share a short SOW draft and estimated engineering days?

Attachments: redwood_vector_integration_requirements.pdf (high-level requirements), poc_scope-draft.docx (initial POC draft).

Proposed timing: Technical kickoff next week (Feb 24–26). Please reply with your preferred time slots and technical contact if different from the people on this thread.

Thanks — looking forward to coordinating.

Hi Camila (and team),

Thanks — excited to collaborate. Quick answers inline below and a couple notes on the POC.

1) Auth: Pinecone supports API keys for service-to-service connections; we recommend rotating keys via your KMS and using IP allowlists for higher assurance. For private deployments we can provide VPC endpoints; I'll loop in our infra contact if we go that route.

2) Throughput: For 50–200 QPS with 512 token-like embeddings, plan for a standard production index backed by replica set; we can share benchmark numbers but typical cost/latency trade-offs depend on index type (sparse ANN vs HNSW), shard sizing, and whether you enable disk-based shards.

3) POC: We can provide a 2-week integration assist (engineering + architecture office hours) and a sandbox index for Redwood to validate routing and fallbacks.

Technical contact: Liam O'Connor (me) and cc'ing Mikayla Ruiz <mikayla@pinecone.io> (solutions infra).

I'll attach a sample auth snippet for server-side use (pinecone_auth_example.json).

Available for kickoff Feb 25 between 11:00–14:00 PT.

Best,

Thanks, Camila. A few engineering notes from the infra side after a quick read-through of the attachment:

- Auth & network: For Redwood-hosted inference we prefer short-lived service tokens issued by our internal KMS and rotated automatically. If partners support either IP allowlist or mTLS that's ideal for Dedicated customers behind VPCs.
- Cold storage pattern: S3 as a cold-tier with object keys mapped to vector IDs + periodic re-hydration to the vector DB works best for very large corpora. We'll want an indexing controller that can reconcile missing IDs in vector DB vs S3.
- Consistency: Expect eventual consistency on upserts for some ANN backends; POC should include obsoletion/ttl strategy tests.
- Observability: We need partner support for per-request tracing headers so we can correlate latency in Redwood Console (trace ids).

POC asks from infra:
- Provide a test index and an API key scoped to read/write for a sandbox environment.
- Sample ingest script (Python) and a sample dataset ~50k items for perf testing.
- SLA-like expectations: sample QPS and 95th percentile latency at target embedding sizes.

I can own the Redwood infra side of the POC. Rafael, Vivek — we'll need a product/sales framing for partner go-to-market outcomes.

— Laura Bennett
